items.title: Pacifying and Thoroughly Pacifying: From the Ten Marks to the Subtler Hindrances

items.zh: 云何寂靜？謂有種種欲恚害等諸惡尋思、貪欲蓋等諸隨煩惱，令心擾動，故彼先應取彼諸法為過患想。由如是想增上力故，於諸尋思及隨煩惱，止息其心，不令流散，故名寂靜。
items.en: What is pacifying? That is, various unwholesome discursive thoughts — of desire, ill will, harm, and the rest — and various secondary afflictions such as the hindrance of craving, cause the mind to become agitated. One should therefore first take these states as objects of the perception of their danger. Through the empowering force of this perception, one calms the mind with respect to these discursive thoughts and secondary afflictions and does not allow it to stray — hence it is called pacifying.

items.zh: 云何名為最極寂靜？謂失念故，即彼二種暫現行時，隨所生起諸惡尋思及隨煩惱，能不忍受，尋即斷滅、除遣、變吐，是故名為最極寂靜。
items.en: What is called thorough pacification? That is, owing to a lapse of mindfulness, when these two kinds — discursive thoughts and secondary afflictions — momentarily manifest, one cannot bear to tolerate whatever arises, and immediately cuts it off, dispels it, and expels it entirely. Hence it is called thorough pacification.

items.title: Section: Single-Pointed Continuity and Equipoise — the Nine Stages Complete

items.zh: 云何名為專注一趣？謂有加行、有功用、無缺無間三摩地相續而住，是故名為專注一趣。云何等持？謂數修、數習、數多修習為因緣故，得無加行、無功用任運轉道。由是因緣，不由加行、不由功用，心三摩地任運相續，無散亂轉，故名等持。
items.en: What is called single-pointed continuity? That is, with effort and application, samādhi continues to abide without lapse and without interruption — hence it is called single-pointed continuity. What is equipoise? That is, through the causes and conditions of repeated cultivation, repeated practice, and extensive repeated practice, one attains a path that proceeds spontaneously, without effort and without application. Owing to this, without effort and without application, the mind's samādhi continues spontaneously, proceeding without distraction — hence it is called equipoise.

items.title: Section: Six Powers That Accomplish the Nine Stages

items.zh: 當知此中，由六種力，方能成辦九種心住。一、聽聞力，二、思惟力，三、憶念力，四、正知力，五、精進力，六、串習力。
items.en: Know that herein, it is through six powers that the nine stages of mental abiding are actually accomplished. First, the power of hearing. Second, the power of reflection. Third, the power of mindful recollection. Fourth, the power of clear comprehension. Fifth, the power of diligence. Sixth, the power of habituation.

items.zh: 初由聽聞、思惟二力，數聞數思增上力故，最初令心於內境住，及即於此相續方便、澄淨方便，等遍安住。如是於內繫縛心已，由憶念力、數數作意攝錄其心，令不散亂，安住、近住。從此已後，由正知力調息其心，於其諸相、諸惡尋思、諸隨煩惱，不令流散，調順、寂靜。由精進力，設彼二種暫現行時，能不忍受，尋即斷滅、除遣、變吐，最極寂靜、專注一趣。由串習力，等持成滿。

items.title: Four Kinds of Mental Engagement, Spanning Both Calm-Abiding and Insight

items.zh: 即於如是九種心住，當知復有四種作意。一、力勵運轉作意，二、有間缺運轉作意，三、無間缺運轉作意，四、無功用運轉作意。於內住、等住中，有力勵運轉作意；於安住、近住、調順、寂靜、最極寂靜中，有有間缺運轉作意；於專注一趣中，有無間缺運轉作意；於等持中，有無功用運轉作意。
items.en: Within these same nine stages of mental abiding, know there are also four kinds of mental engagement: first, engagement proceeding through exertion; second, engagement proceeding with interruption; third, engagement proceeding without interruption; fourth, engagement proceeding without effort. Within inward abiding and continuous abiding, there is engagement through exertion. Within patched-together abiding, close abiding, taming, pacifying, and thorough pacification, there is engagement with interruption. Within single-pointed continuity, there is engagement without interruption. Within equipoise, there is engagement without effort.

items.zh: 當知如是四種作意，於九種心住中，是奢摩他品。又即如是獲得內心奢摩他者，於毘鉢舍那勤修習時，復即由是四種作意，方能修習毘鉢舍那，故此亦是毘鉢舍那品。
items.en: Know that these four kinds of mental engagement, within the nine stages of mental abiding, belong to the calm-abiding type. Further, one who has thereby attained inward calm-abiding, when diligently cultivating insight, likewise depends on these same four kinds of engagement in order to actually cultivate insight — hence these belong to the insight type as well.

items.title: Section: The Four Kinds of Wisdom-Conduct Defined — the Insight Track Named

items.zh: 云何四種毘鉢舍那？謂有苾芻，依止內心奢摩他故，於諸法中能正思擇、最極思擇、周遍尋思、周遍伺察，是名四種毘鉢舍那。
items.en: What are the four kinds of insight? That is, a monk, relying on inward calm-abiding, is able, with respect to various phenomena, to discern correctly, discern to the utmost, thoroughly investigate, and thoroughly examine. These are called the four kinds of insight.

items.zh: 云何名為能正思擇？謂於淨行所緣境界、或於善巧所緣境界、或於淨惑所緣境界，能正思擇盡所有性。云何名為最極思擇？謂即於彼所緣境界，最極思擇如所有性。云何名為周遍尋思？謂即於彼所緣境界，由慧俱行有分別作意，取彼相狀，周遍尋思。云何名為周遍伺察？謂即於彼所緣境界，審諦推求，周遍伺察。
items.en: What is called discerning correctly? That is, with respect to objects for purifying conduct, or objects of skilful means, or objects for purifying affliction, being able to discern correctly their full extent of particular characteristics. What is called discerning to the utmost? That is, with respect to that same object, discerning to the utmost its universal characteristics as they truly are. What is called thoroughly investigating? That is, with respect to that same object, through discernment-accompanied, deliberate mental engagement, grasping its features and thoroughly investigating them. What is called thoroughly examining? That is, with respect to that same object, carefully and truthfully seeking it out, thoroughly examining it.

items.zh: 又即如是毘鉢舍那，由三門、六事差別所緣，當知復有多種差別。

items.title: Three Gates of Insight: From Bare Repetition to Genuine Examination

items.zh: 云何三門毘鉢舍那？一、唯隨相行毘鉢舍那，二、隨尋思行毘鉢舍那，三、隨伺察行毘鉢舍那。云何名為唯隨相行毘鉢舍那？謂於所聞所受持法，或於教授教誡諸法，由等引地如理作意，暫爾思惟，未思、未量、未推、未察。如是名為唯隨相行毘鉢舍那。若復於彼思量推察，爾時名為隨尋思行毘鉢舍那。若復於彼既推察已，如所安立復審觀察，如是名為隨伺察行毘鉢舍那。是名三門毘鉢舍那。
items.en: What are the three gates of insight? First, insight that merely follows the mark. Second, insight that follows investigation. Third, insight that follows examination. What is insight that merely follows the mark? That is, with respect to teachings one has heard and upheld, or to instructions and guidance received, one briefly reflects upon them, through sound-reasoning attention within concentrative equipoise, without yet having deliberated, weighed, inferred, or examined them — this is called insight that merely follows the mark. If one goes on to deliberate and infer upon it, this is then called insight that follows investigation. If, having already inferred upon it, one further carefully observes it as thus established, this is called insight that follows examination.

blocks.text: The last stages of calm, the powers that accomplish them, and the beginning of insight. A short passage (0451a22) is untranslated.

Unwholesome thoughts (of desire, ill will, harm) and hindrances: seeing their faults, one does not let the mind follow them. **Thorough pacification**: when, through lapse of mindfulness, they momentarily appear, "one cannot bear to tolerate them, and immediately cuts them off".

**Single-pointed continuity**: "with effort and application, samādhi continues without lapse". **Equipoise**: "without effort, the mind's samādhi continues spontaneously". Compare the four kinds of attention on Day 242.

Hearing and reflection (the first two stages), mindful recollection (the third and fourth), clear comprehension (fifth and sixth), diligence (seventh and eighth), and thorough habituation (the ninth). Master Cháng Bǎi: such careful explanation "is rarely seen elsewhere".
Through exertion (the first two stages); interrupted (the next five); uninterrupted (the eighth); effortless (the ninth). These belong to the calm type.

Relying on inner calm, one "discerns correctly, discerns to the utmost, thoroughly investigates, and thoroughly scrutinises" phenomena. Correct discernment concerns the "exhaustive particulars"; utmost discernment, their "universal nature" (Day 224).
Insight that merely follows the mark; that follows investigation; that follows examination. Venerable Miào Jìng: the equipoise needed here is that of the absorptions.

quiz.q: How do taming and pacifying differ in what they counter, according to the masters?
options: Miào Jìng: in pacifying the senses no longer meet objects, only the sixth stirs; Cháng Bǎi: disturbance is the ten sense marks plus the sixth's eight thoughts and five hindrances
quiz.why: "Various unwholesome discursive thoughts — of desire, ill will, harm — and secondary afflictions such as the hindrance of craving cause the mind to become agitated." Venerable Miào Jìng: the five senses no longer contact their objects; only the sixth consciousness is active while sitting. Master Cháng Bǎi: disturbance is nothing but the ten marks of the five senses plus the eight discursive thoughts and five hindrances of the sixth.

quiz.q: What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use for 注 in "single-pointed continuity"?
options: water dripping from the eaves, every drop on the same spot
quiz.why: "With effort and application, samādhi continues to abide without lapse and without interruption — hence it is called single-pointed continuity." Venerable Miào Jìng: 注 is a simile — water dripping from the eaves drop by drop, all on that one spot.

quiz.q: Equipoise "continues spontaneously without effort." What does Venerable Miào Jìng warn about this desire-realm concentration?
options: hard to gain, easy to lose — one quarrel and it's gone
quiz.why: "Without effort and without application, the mind's samādhi continues spontaneously, proceeding without distraction — hence it is called equipoise." Venerable Miào Jìng: this desire-realm concentration is hard to gain and easy to lose; quarrel with someone and it's gone at once.

quiz.q: What are the six powers that accomplish the nine stages, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng explain mindful recollection?
options: hearing, reflection, recollection, comprehension, diligence, habituation; recollection makes the object vividly present without further thought
quiz.why: "First, the power of hearing. Second, the power of reflection. Third, the power of mindful recollection. Fourth, the power of clear comprehension. Fifth, the power of diligence. Sixth, the power of habituation." Venerable Miào Jìng: recollection is making the object appear distinctly in the mind, without adding other thought.

quiz.q: Inward and continuous abiding involve engagement through exertion. Does Master Cháng Bǎi count it among the seven engagements?
options: a preliminary to the seven, not yet one of them
quiz.why: "Within inward abiding and continuous abiding, there is engagement through exertion." Master Cháng Bǎi: forceful engagement is a preliminary to the seven engagements, not yet one of them.

quiz.q: What are the four kinds of insight, and what image does Master Cháng Bǎi use for examining?
options: discern, discern utmost, investigate, examine; examining is like a cat watching a mousehole
quiz.why: "Able, with respect to various phenomena, to discern correctly, discern to the utmost, thoroughly investigate, and thoroughly examine. These are called the four kinds of insight." Master Cháng Bǎi: like a cat catching a mouse, intently guarding the hole, peering, probing, patrolling.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "gate" in "three gates of insight"?
options: a gate lets one go in and out — such contemplation leads from the ordinary to the noble
quiz.why: "What are the three gates of insight? First, insight that merely follows the mark. Second, insight that follows investigation. Third, insight that follows examination." Master Cháng Bǎi: a gate means entering and exiting — by contemplating this way one can pass from the ordinary person's state into the noble one's.
